title: Smooth image of iterated Frobenius for affine algebraic groups
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $G$ be an affine group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Smoothness means smoothness of the structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, then $G$ is smooth. If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, there is an integer $r\geq1$ such that the scheme-theoretic image $I$ of the relative Frobenius $F^r_{G/k}:G\to G^{(p^r)}$ is a smooth affine group scheme of finite type over $k$. Here $G^{(p^r)}=G\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k,F_k^r}\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the base change [def-pc-fibre-product] along the field map $a\mapsto a^{p^r}$, and on coordinate rings the relative Frobenius is $k[G]\otimes_{k,a\mapsto a^{p^r}}k\to k[G]$, $b\otimes c\mapsto cb^{p^r}$. Scheme-theoretic image here means $I=\operatorname{Spec}(k[G^{(p^r)}]/\ker((F^r_{G/k})^*))$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The resulting factorization is by homomorphisms of group schemes $G\xrightarrow{u}I\xrightarrow{j}G^{(p^r)}$, with $j$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $j\circ u=F^r_{G/k}$.

source.place: Theorem 3.23 (Cartier), printed p.71; Proposition 3.29 and Remark 3.30, printed pp.72--73, including the group-scheme image factorization.

proof.text: Put $A=k[G]$. By [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf], the pullbacks of multiplication, identity and inverse make $A$ a commutative Hopf $k$-algebra, with maps $\Delta,\epsilon,S$, and identify its spectrum group with $G$. By [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra], $A$ is finitely generated over $k$. These are the hypotheses needed for the reduced-core lemma.

source.place: Proposition 3.6 and Corollary 3.7, pp.66--67; finite generation is the affine finite-type dictionary (Stacks 01T2).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-hopf-reduced-core-nilpotent-fibre] to $A$. It supplies a finitely generated reduced Hopf subalgebra $C\subseteq A$, with the restricted structure maps. In characteristic zero choose $C=A$; in characteristic $p>0$ choose $r\geq1$ with $C=\{a^{p^r}:a\in A\}$. Only these conclusions are used, not the lemma's extra nilpotent-fibre conclusion. By [lem-sfb-hopf-spectrum-functor], $H=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is an affine group scheme. It is of finite type: a finite algebra generating family for $C$ gives the one-member affine cover in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-reduced-iff], $H$ is reduced.

source.place: Theorem 3.23 and Proposition 3.29, pp.71--73; Proposition 3.6, p.66.

proof.text: The field $k$ is perfect: this is automatic in characteristic zero, while in characteristic $p$ every $c\in k$ has a $p$th root because $T^p-c$ has a root in the algebraically closed field. Thus [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect] applies to the reduced finite-type scheme $H$ and makes it geometrically reduced. The group-scheme smoothness theorem [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth] now makes $H$ smooth. If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, the choice $C=A$ identifies $H$ with $G$ and proves the first clause. For the rest assume $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$ and retain the chosen $r$.

source.place: Proposition 1.28, p.14, and Remark 3.30, p.73; geometric reducedness over a perfect field is Stacks 020I (varieties, lemma-perfect-reduced).

proof.text: Set $q=p^r$ and $B=A\otimes_{k,\lambda\mapsto\lambda^q}k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $\operatorname{Spec}B=G^{(q)}$ with its stated structure map. Define $\varphi:B\to A$ by $b\otimes c\mapsto cb^q$. This is a $k$-algebra map by the tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]: $b\mapsto b^q$ is additive and multiplicative in characteristic $p$, and the balancing relation $(\lambda b)\otimes c=b\otimes\lambda^q c$ has the same image on both sides. Its image is exactly $C$: it contains every $b^q=\varphi(b\otimes1)$; conversely each $\varphi(\sum_i b_i\otimes c_i)=\sum_i c_i b_i^q$ lies in the $k$-subalgebra $C$. Write $\bar\varphi:B\twoheadrightarrow C$ for its corestriction and $i:C\hookrightarrow A$ for inclusion.

source.place: Sections 2.24--2.28, pp.46--48; Proposition 3.29, pp.72--73, identification of the coordinate-ring image.

proof.text: The group structure on $G^{(q)}$ is obtained by base changing that of $G$: its diagrams remain equal after base change. On coordinates the Hopf maps on $B$ are the corresponding scalar extensions. If $\Delta(b)=\sum_i b_i'\otimes b_i''$, their compatibility with $\varphi$ is the identity $\Delta(cb^q)=c\sum_i(b_i')^q\otimes(b_i'')^q$; the other two identities are $\epsilon(cb^q)=c\epsilon(b)^q$ and $S(cb^q)=cS(b)^q$. Here [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf] supplies multiplicativity of the three maps. These equalities on pure tensors imply equality on $B$. The map $\bar\varphi$ preserves the restricted Hopf maps on $C$: the same equalities hold in $C$ and $C\otimes_kC$, the latter injecting into $A\otimes_kA$ by extending a $k$-basis of $C$ to one of $A$. The inclusion $i$ is Hopf by step 2. By [lem-sfb-hopf-spectrum-functor], $u_H=\operatorname{Spec}i:G\to H$ and $j_H=\operatorname{Spec}\bar\varphi:H\to G^{(q)}$ are group homomorphisms and $j_Hu_H=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi=F^r_{G/k}$.

source.place: Sections 2.27--2.28, pp.48--49, and Propositions 3.6 and 3.9, pp.66--67; explicit verification of the Frobenius homomorphism.

proof.text: The map $B/\ker\varphi\to C$, $b+\ker\varphi\mapsto\varphi(b)$, is well defined and injective because two representatives have the same image exactly when their difference belongs to $\ker\varphi$; it is surjective by step 4. It preserves the $k$-algebra operations, so it is an isomorphism. Contravariant functoriality of [def-weil-affine-spectrum] therefore identifies the specified scheme-theoretic image $I=\operatorname{Spec}(B/\ker\varphi)$ with $H$. Give $I$ the group structure through this isomorphism, and use it to identify $u_H,j_H$ with $u,j$; the composition equality and the homomorphism properties persist under this identification. The map $j$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion], since on the single affine chart of $G^{(q)}$ its coordinate map is the surjection $B\to B/\ker\varphi$. Finally $I\cong H$ is affine, finite type and smooth by steps 2--3. This proves every positive-characteristic clause.

source.place: Remark 3.30, p.73, image factorization; the quotient/image identification is written out, and the affine closed-immersion criterion is Stacks 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion).

proof_origin.place: Propositions 3.6, 3.9 and 3.29, Theorem 3.23 and Remark 3.30; Sections 2.24--2.28 for relative Frobenius. Existing reduced-core lemma supplies the algebraic smoothening input.
